title: Kernel Sage: seqlen & architecture advisory autotuner
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our serving runtime currently uses a mix of static heuristics and ad-hoc warmstarts to pick kernels for attention and matmul paths. This leads to suboptimal latency/cost tradeoffs for heterogeneous hardware (A100/V100/RTX) and mixed-length conversational loads where prefill and decode phases diverge.

Goal: Build an advisor/autotuner—'Kernel Sage'—that recommends and adapts kernel choices per-architecture and per-sequence-length distribution, safely rolls out changes, and integrates with prefill/decode schedulers to reduce unit cost while keeping latency SLOs. The Sage should be lightweight at admission time, work with existing microprobe harnesses, and provide deterministic fallbacks.

Approach: 1) Feature fingerprinting: derive a compact per-request fingerprint: hardware SKU, tensor shapes, seqlen histogram (from recent window), token-phase indicator (prefill vs decode), batch size, quantization profile. 2) Offline candidate pool: compile a small candidate set of kernels for each op variant (attention, ffn, matmul) per-arch using microbenchmarks. Store performance vectors (latency, throughput, memory, measured variance) in an index. 3) Per-request advisor: lightweight cost model that scores candidates by expected latency cost per token and probability of SLO violation; combine historical priors with small online probes when cold. 4) Autotune loop: Bayesian bandit with constrained objective (minimize cost subject to latency P95 < SLO + safety margin). Use conservative exploration with decaying temperature and simulated rollback if real traffic shows degradations. 5) Integration: advisor plugs into admission control and scheduling: prefill requests may bias toward high-throughput kernels, decode toward low-latency kernels; support hybrid pipelines that split prefill/decode across kernel variants where safe. 6) Telemetry & safety: capture P50/P95/P99 latency, token cost, error rates, kernel-switch frequency, and per-candidate variance; automatic alarms and automated canary rollback policies. 7) Rollout: staged canary by customer tier and region, then traffic percentage ramps.

Acceptance criteria: - 10% reduction in token unit cost on mixed conversational workloads in internal benchmark suite without increasing P95 beyond 5% of baseline. - No customer-facing SLO breaches during canaries. - Clear telemetry showing kernel-selection decisions and the reasoning scores. - Add e2e test in runtime CI that validates advisor respects fallback and rollback rules.

Implementation notes: - Leverage existing microprobe harness (ENG-712908) to generate candidate performance profiles. - Store candidate catalog in the runtime metadata service with TTL and versioning so rollbacks are trivial. - Expose advisor decisions in request traces for debugging. - Keep admission-time fingerprint and scoring under 50us added latency.

Out-of-scope: full per-token re-evaluation inside generators (future work). Quantization-specific kernel fusion tuning is separate (tracked elsewhere).
comments: 2026-01-20: Ticket created by Aisha. Initial design doc attached to doc link: (confluence/runtime/kernel-sage).

2026-01-28: Design review with runtime and infra: agreed on compact fingerprint schema and conservative bayesian bandit for exploration. Action: prototype scorer and offline microbench catalog. (Miguel O.).

2026-02-10: Prototype: microbench harness produced candidate latency table for A100/RTX across seqlen buckets 8/32/128/512. Early results show 7-12% token cost variance between best and baseline kernels depending on seqlen. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/PR-4382).

2026-02-24: Safety: added explicit P95 margin parameter and canary controller design. Security review flagged data retention for per-request fingerprints; design updated to hash and TTL fingerprints. (security follow-up planned).

2026-03-03: Integration: advisor hook implemented in admission path; add-only toggle behind feature flag runtime.kernel_sage.enabled. Local perf: scoring adds ~22us median overhead. Need optimization to reach 50us SLA. (WIP).
2026-03-10: Ready for small internal canary: create canary cohorts and dashboard. Next: telemetry sanitization, add e2e CI test, plan rollout schedule for runtime-1.20.
